correctness.rationale: For the unweighted adjacency walk, time averaging keeps exactly the equal-eigenvalue terms. The quadratic form is the sum of squared Frobenius norms of the compressions E_lambda diag(z) E_lambda, so all compressions must vanish. The center-coupled block is a symmetric arrowhead with nonzero couplings at odd path eigenvalues, hence simple and disjoint from those poles. At an even mode lambda its reflection-symmetric path resolvent has coordinate sum (m+1)/(lambda-2), so collision would require lambda(lambda-2)=b(m+1), impossible since the left side is less than 8 and the right at least 9. Thus the even path space is unrestricted in the blade index and each odd path space has blade sum zero. Testing single blades and then blade differences forces every squared-sine moment to vanish per blade (for three or more blades each pair-sum vanishes and hence every entry vanishes). The Fourier transform of the symmetric part extended with a zero at index 0 is constant by sin^2=(1-cos(2x))/2, forcing that part to be zero. A coupled eigenvector with nonzero center enforces z_0=0, and products within each spectrally separated eigenspace are reflection-symmetric on each blade, proving the converse. Counting pairs gives the stated rank and nullity including m=2. The attached NumPy projector/rank script and recorded 40 graph cases were inspected, not run; the proof handles exact multiplicities without tolerance assumptions.
